title: Quiz: Greenhouse Gases and Climate Change

options.text: The trapping of heat energy (infrared radiation) by gases in the atmosphere, keeping the Earth warm
The destruction of the ozone layer by pollutants
The heating of greenhouses by the Sun
The cooling of the Earth by clouds reflecting sunlight

questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is a natural process where greenhouse gases in the atmosphere absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, trapping heat and keeping the Earth warm enough to support life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is not a greenhouse gas. The main greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapour. Nitrogen makes up 78% of the atmosphere but does not absorb infrared radiation.

questions.stem: What human activity is the largest contributor to increased carbon dioxide levels?

options.text: Burning fossil fuels for energy and transport

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, and natural gas) for energy, transport, and industry is the largest source of increased atmospheric carbon dioxide, as it releases carbon that was locked away for millions of years.

questions.stem: Which greenhouse gas is released by cattle farming and decomposing waste in landfill?
questions.explanation: Methane is produced by cattle (from digestion) and by the anaerobic decomposition of waste in landfill sites. It is a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide, although present in smaller quantities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a potential consequence of global climate change?

options.text: Rising sea levels due to melting polar ice caps
The atmosphere losing all its oxygen

questions.explanation: Rising sea levels caused by the melting of polar ice caps and thermal expansion of seawater is a well-documented consequence of climate change. Other effects include more extreme weather events and changes to ecosystems.

questions.stem: Why is the enhanced greenhouse effect a concern?

options.text: Because it makes the atmosphere contain less nitrogen
Because increased levels of greenhouse gases are causing average global temperatures to rise
Because it reduces the amount of sunlight reaching Earth
Because it causes the ozone layer to get thicker

questions.explanation: The enhanced greenhouse effect refers to the additional warming caused by increased concentrations of greenhouse gases from human activities. This is causing global temperatures to rise, leading to climate change.

questions.stem: What type of evidence do scientists use to show that climate change is occurring?

options.text: Ice core data, sea level measurements, temperature records, and changes in wildlife patterns
Only temperature readings from the last 10 years

questions.explanation: Scientists use multiple sources of evidence including ice core data (which reveals past atmospheric composition), long-term temperature records, sea level measurements, and observed changes in ecosystems and weather patterns.
